correctness.rationale: Use the 1-dimensional graph spine for ordered p-point configurations on a star with m≥3 arms: an A-vertex specifies one ordered queue of distinct labels per arm, a B-vertex selects central particle c and queues other labels, and each B-state has one edge per destination arm by prepending c. Recalling the central/relative radial ordering construction, it is natural under permutations of identically parameterized arms (not merely a nonequivariant homotopy equivalence); the arm group acts on the model graph with no edge inversion, hence the geometric configuration quotient is homotopy equivalent to a connected quotient graph. For g fixing f arms, only fixed arms may carry queues: fixed A=R_p(f), B=pR_{p−1}(f), and edges=fpR_{p−1}(f); Burnside averaging vertex and edge orbits gives the exact displayed β_p(H). For H=S_m, queue-multiset orbit states (plus marking one edge target) stabilize as graphs when m≥p, and are all realized at that threshold. The falling-factorial leading coefficient −(p−1) of [2p−1−(p−1)f]R_{p−1}(f) and E[(fixedpoints)_j]=1 for j≤m establish β_p(S_p)−β_p(S_{p−1})=p−1; independently evaluated exact averages for p=4..8, reproducing jumps 3..7 and stable ranks 12,180,2220,27300,351960. Finite cases only corroborate all-p,m algebra.

originality.rationale: The cited star-configuration spine and nonequivariant free-group rank are established prior work; Ramos–Yun Theorem 3.3 computes only p=2 rational S_m representations of the unquotiented ordered and unordered configurations. Neither such representations nor Wawrykow's homology generators determine geometric orbit-space graph rank for every p≥4 and every H≤S_m, nor a sharp graph-poset stabilization boundary. The fixed-arm subgroup formula and sharpness appear new among inspected primary sources, subject to alternative equivariant model risk.
residual_risks: Relies on arm-permutation naturality of the canonical queue graph deformation retraction; the primary spine theorem is often stated with particle-permutation equivariance, so the cellwise arm-naturality argument should remain explicit.
Only ordinary orbit homotopy is claimed, not integral equivariant module classification, particle-label quotient or non-star graphs.
Other treatments of automorphism quotients in graph-braid literature may exist under different terms.
